record.context_brief: Normalized local length of full Steiner trees
record.original_question: Let St ⊂ Rd with d > 2, and additionally assume that St is full. What is the maximum possible value of H1(St ∩ Btr(x)) / r for t ∈ (0, 1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d>2$ and let $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a Steiner tree, that is, a connected set that is the union of finitely many straight line segments meeting only at their endpoints, having no cycles. Call $S$ full if every vertex of $S$ that is not a leaf has degree exactly $3$ and the three segments meeting at each such vertex form pairwise angles of $120^\circ$ (equivalently, $S$ is a full Steiner tree in the classical sense, with no "Steiner point" of degree less than $3$ and no terminal of degree greater than $1$).

For a point $x\in S$ and a radius $r>0$, write $B_r(x)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:|y-x|<r\}$ and let $\mathcal{H}^1$ denote one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (i.e., total length).

Fix a parameter $t\in(0,1)$. Determine the supremum, over all full Steiner trees $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, all points $x\in S$, and all radii $r>0$ with $B_r(x)$ containing only finitely many segments of $S$ in a controlled way, of the quantity
$$\frac{\mathcal{H}^1\bigl(S\cap B_{tr}(x)\bigr)}{r}.$$
In other words, find the largest possible value (as a function of $t$ and $d$) of the normalized local length $\mathcal{H}^1(S\cap B_{tr}(x))/r$ for full Steiner trees in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d>2$.
artifact.category_tag: Steiner trees and geometric measure theory
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about the maximum normalized local length of full Steiner trees in dimensions greater than two. A web search did not surface a published resolution; analogous monotonicity/length-density bounds for Steiner trees in higher dimensions appear to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Approximate Euclidean Steiner Trees
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses full ε-approximate Steiner trees in R^d and related monotonicity properties without resolving the local length-density question.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit formula for the maximum of H^1(S ∩ B_{tr}(x))/r for full Steiner trees in R^d, d>2, is given.
